subject: Intrinsic functions
notes: PARTIAL -> CONFORMS (kb/Work PB251, landed). The refuter kept this row PARTIAL for exactly three reasons and all three are now closed. (a) CORRECTION 1 -- the exception 'unless otherwise specified in the function definition' was NOT honoured for NUMVAL / NUMVAL-C under NATIVE arithmetic: 15.67.4 r1 / 15.68.4 r1 state 'The returned value is the numeric value represented by argument-1' with no arithmetic-mode qualification, and neither function has an equivalent arithmetic expression, so the closing sentence's latitude is withdrawn in every mode -- yet the native lane materialized the value at ws = max(receiver scale, 6) fraction digits. MEASURED before the fix on this tree's own cobol.exe: DISPLAY FUNCTION NUMVAL("0.1234567") -> 0.123456; DISPLAY FUNCTION NUMVAL-C("$0.1234567","$") -> 0.123456; and a receiver was no protection, because it bounds the STATEMENT's result and not an OPERAND's precision -- COMPUTE R = FUNCTION NUMVAL("0.1234567") * 10000000 stored 1234560 into PIC 9(9) where r1 owes 1234567. FIXED at the root: RenderNum routes NUMVAL and NUMVAL-C to the SDIDI projection BEFORE the arithmetic-mode dispatch, and the native working-scale case arms are deleted -- 15.4.1 leaves the implementor only 'the characteristics and representation of the returned value', and the SDIDI is the one representation that holds every 15.67.3 r3-conforming argument (31 digits native, 34 standard) with no working scale, its exponent being carried at run time. No compile-time scale could have done it: a scaled Int128 needs i + ws digits and r3 permits i = 31, so the only ws safe for every conforming argument is 7, while NUMVAL("0.123456789") needs 9. NUMVAL-F is deliberately NOT moved -- 15.69.4 r2 grants native arithmetic 'an approximation of the numeric value represented by argument-1', which is why r3 states the standard-decimal value separately. (b) The SQRT half of the exception is closed at HEAD by kb/Work PB116 (RenderDec's alwaysDec names Sqrt; the SqrtDec arm carries 15.84.4 r2's 34 digits). (c) CORRECTION 2 leaned on RV-15.4.1-2 and RV-15.4.1-3 both standing at PARTIAL; RV-15.4.1-3 is CONFORMS since kb/Work PB167 landed, and RV-15.4.1-2 is CONFORMS in this same batch. EVIDENCE: conformance:cases/15.4.1-Numeric-and-integer-functions/pb251_numval_native_value_fixed is the NATIVE twin of pb60_numval_standard_decimal -- fifteen of its lines are byte-identical to the standard-decimal golden's for the same references, which is the row's rule stated as a test, plus I31/D31 (31 digits at either end of the decimal separator, the two ends no single working scale can serve at once), C32 (the 32nd digit exceeds 15.67.3 r3 -> EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION, checking off -> 15.3 r14's implementor-defined result 0) and RAWF (NUMVAL-F's r2 approximation, the contrast that must not move). unit:IntrinsicArgumentIntakeContractDriftTests.NumvalFamily_HasNoCompileTimeWorkingScale asserts the ABSENCE of a working-scale render for the family and that the value-fixed arm precedes the mode branch; CarrierLandingFormTests now asserts no case "Numval"/"NumvalC" arm exists at all. Three now-unreachable Int128 value projections (CobolIntrinsics.Numval, .NumvalC, .NumvalCLocale) were deleted rather than left as a second copy of the rule -- PB60 fixed one projection of this family and left the other wrong, and that is the shape this row records. Citations re-checked with cite.py --check: 15.4.1 closing sentence OK, 15.4.1 native characteristics/representation OK, 15.67.4 r1 OK, 15.67.4 r2 OK, 15.67.3 r2 OK, 15.67.3 r3 OK, 15.67.3 r4 OK, 15.68.4 r1 OK, 15.69.4 r2 OK, 15.3 r14 OK. EDITIONS: unchanged batch default -- the closing sentence is mode- and edition-neutral and governs every intrinsic function from the '85 catalog onward.
